reason: The text contains two named characters who are depicted as regular people (human beings): Adam (הָֽאָדָם, explicitly referred to by this name throughout) and Eve (חַוָּ֑ה, explicitly named when Adam calls his wife by this name: 'וַיִּקְרָא הָֽאָדָ֛ם שֵׁ֥ם אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ חַוָּ֑ה'). Both are portrayed as human beings with human characteristics: they speak, reason, make decisions, experience emotions, engage in labor, form relationships, and have agency. Though they exist in a supernatural context (the Garden of Eden) and directly interact with God, they are fundamentally depicted as human persons, not divine or purely allegorical figures.
